items.text: Sam row, C5: 'before Friday' is in the memo as 2026-10-09; strict reading gives 2026-10-08. Reviewer: 'The memo's 2026-10-09 is correct only under reading 1.'

Marta row, C5: 'book the on-call training room for Oct 14'. Memo has Due none with 2026-10-14 in the Action text; alternative is Due 2026-10-14. Reviewer: 'Oct 14 is the training date, no deadline for the booking' vs 'Oct 14 is the Due date'.
Lee row, C5: 'this week ... no hard date attached'. Memo has Due none; alternative 2026-10-09. Reviewer advises none.

C3: requester asked for an 'Open questions' section, but C3 allows only Decisions and Actions. I put the explanations in the Sam and Marta Action cells. Reviewer: 'C3 does not say whether an Action cell may hold non-action text; I do not decide it.' Alternative: keep Action cells to the action only and drop the explanations.

C7 (reviewer: 'needs my report to show n = m and the writer to have applied all changes. It is circular for me to certify'): does C7 count as met when the review has no required changes and every other criterion passes?
Sam staging row (C4): notes say he "will probably sort it out himself"; hedged. Kept as a commitment, Due 2026-10-21 (day before the 22 Oct freeze). Reviewer: "Criteria do not settle it."
Lee pager swap (C3): "Nobody had a problem with that"; row kept (Due none), no Decisions bullet. Reviewer: AMBIGUOUS whether it is a decision.
RFC decision (C3): one bullet covers approve-with-token-bucket and ship-behind-flag-first; reviewer: could be read as two decisions.
Lee Due (C5): none vs "demo week"; reviewer judges none correct, no date stated.

R2/C9: 'Owners as initials only, always' vs C9 limited to the Owner column. The Lee row's Action cell still says 'Swap pager shifts with Dev for the demo week' (reviewer: ambiguous; fix would be 'with D'). Kept as is.
Sam row (C4/C5): 'will probably sort it out himself' is hedged; kept as a commitment, Due 2026-10-21 per your ruling.
Lee swap (C3/C4): 'Nobody had a problem with that' not treated as a separate decision; Lee row Due none ('demo week' is a period, C5), per your ruling.
RFC bullet (C3): bundles two decisions (approve with token bucket; ship behind flag first) in one bullet, per your ruling.
C7 wording: the reviewer's n of m lists C1-C6, C8, C9 only. Suggest C7 read 'reviewer coverage line for C1-C6, C8, C9 has n = m'.
C4: Marta 'will keep the agenda as sent' left out. Reviewer: 'fits C4's wording commitment ... C4 can be read both ways. I do not decide.'
C4: Sam's offer to pair with Jo included, Due none. Reviewer: '"offered" is not "will"; C4 says informal ones in prose, which supports inclusion.' If excluded, Summary must say four actions.
C5: Lee 'probably by end of next week' kept as Due none. Reviewer: 'hedged relative date ... could be 2026-10-30 on another reading.'
C9: Sam's Action cell names 'Jo' (new hire, not an owner). Reviewer: unclear whether R2 also covers names in Action text.

Next meeting (Monday 2 November) is not listed as an action; C4; reviewer: "Whether the next-meeting date (Monday 2 November) is a commitment: I read it as a scheduling fact, not listed; the memo omits it." Memo kept as verified.

C10: the notes give first names only (Dev, Priya, Marta, Sam, Lee), so Owner shows those as written; surnames would be invention (C6). Reviewer: "If the client expects surnames, the notes don't have them". Please confirm.
C3/C4: next meeting Monday 2 November is left out as a commitment nobody made; the reviewer lists it for completeness.

C10 vs C4: the notes name the owner of the deck action only as 'JD' (initials). A full name cannot come from the notes. Reviewer: 'does JD as written count, or must the client supply a full name?' Please give JD's full name, or rule that JD as written is acceptable. I did not decide it.
R2 ("Owners as initials only, always"), reviewer: "ambiguous. Contradicts R3; ... I cannot judge the supersession myself." Memo kept as verified; please decide.

C10/R3: the notes give owners as first names only (Priya, Sam, Lee, Marta, Dev). Memo uses them as written. Reviewer: "'full name as written in the notes' can mean (a) the name exactly as written, i.e. first name, or (b) a full first+last name, which the notes never give." Which do you want?
R2 vs R3/C10: R2 ("Owners as initials only, always", C9 removed) contradicts R3. Not applied.
C5: Sam's "by Friday" has no stated Friday; memo uses 2026-11-13 (Friday of the meeting week). Reviewer: 2026-11-20 "a possible alternative reading, though less natural."
